report.summary: The release updates how drawings are displayed, navigated, saved, and exported while preserving their content.
keyChanges: On-screen drawing now renders objects from zoom-specific cached canvases; fractional object origins are rounded down to whole canvas units, so their placement can shift by less than one unit.

Scene rendering now reports whether any drawing objects are visible, which the editor uses to track whether the drawing is outside the viewport; rendering also uses scene scroll values instead of separate per-render offsets.
Canvas scrolling and restored centering now use floored positions, so fractional movement or placement is rounded down.
Canvas redraws now enable rendering optimizations, and resizing clears cached shape data before redrawing.
Local saving now includes entries of type “selection”; restored scenes also clear cached rendering data and default missing canvas offsets to 0.
Raster exports now use floored offsets, which can change the padding for drawings whose bounds are fractional.
Copy, undo/redo history, and local saves no longer retain cached canvas data with drawing elements; verify these workflows still preserve the visible drawing.
Canvas-based exports now use floored scroll offsets, so fractional drawing bounds may shift export placement by less than one unit and should not cause artwork to be clipped.

Wheel scrolling, canvas panning, and scrollbar dragging now round each resulting scene offset down to a whole unit, so fractional movement may produce a different viewport position than before. Newly created elements also receive canvas-cache defaults, with no user-visible behavior established by the supplied evidence.

report.summary: The release expands drawing-editor support for creating and managing groups across selection, editing, copying, and restored drawings.
keyChanges: Selecting elements within a group now selects their group, while selection-box drags also include group members; nested groups are resolved relative to the group being edited.
Grouping within an edited group inserts the new group at that nesting level, and duplication now receives the editing-group context to handle group IDs together.
Clicking empty canvas clears group selection and exits group editing; clicking an element while a group is selected no longer clears that selection when no drag occurred.
Double-clicking an element in a selected group now enters group editing instead of starting text entry; clicking outside that group exits editing without selecting the outside element.

Pasted elements made while editing a group now join that group, and changing to a drawing tool, finishing text editing, or releasing Space with a drawing tool active clears group editing and selection.
Restored elements without group metadata now receive an empty group list, so older drawings can be handled by the group-aware editor.
New canvas elements start with no group membership, while copies of grouped elements receive remapped group IDs so duplicated members can remain grouped without reusing the source group.
Select All now exits group editing and selects groups along with all non-deleted elements; duplication and paste use the active group context when remapping memberships.
Selecting two or more elements and pressing Ctrl/Cmd+G groups them; pressing Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+G removes the selected group membership.

A selected group is outlined as a whole rather than giving its grouped elements separate local-selection outlines, and the same group-selection rendering change is used wherever scene rendering is enabled.

report.summary: The release improves whiteboard drawing edits and makes them more reliable.
keyChanges: In the drawing editor, line and arrow points can be dragged, points can be added with Alt-click, and dragging an endpoint near the other endpoint closes a path when it has at least three points.

Point updates with the same number of points are now skipped when their coordinates are unchanged; however, a change to only the first point is also skipped, so that point update may not appear or be recorded.

Replacing drawing elements now refreshes the element lookup map and non-deleted list, supporting actions on newly pasted or otherwise replaced elements. The loop-check change only alters a type annotation and has no runtime behavior change.

Pressing Enter or double-clicking with exactly one line, arrow, or freehand drawing selected now enters point-editing mode; its points are shown as handles, and canvas pointer input is routed to point editing instead of ordinary selection or resizing.

Point editing is finalized when its drawing is no longer selected, and its temporary state is omitted from saved editor state; rendering also suppresses ordinary selection outlines while a linear drawing is being edited.
Editing a line or arrow normalizes its first point to the origin while adjusting its position, and point selection and movement account for the drawing’s rotation.

Alt-dragging in point-edit mode previews a new point, releasing Alt removes an uncommitted preview, and Alt-clicking adds or commits a point; releasing a dragged endpoint can close a loop when the path qualifies as closed.
Resize-handle hit testing now takes the pointer’s scene coordinates as separate values; the supplied evidence does not establish a different user-visible resize result.

Selecting one line, arrow, or free-draw element can now show context-sensitive editing guidance; shortcut names in that guidance and other displays no longer translate CtrlOrCmd, Alt, Del, Enter, or Return when the token is embedded within a larger word.

Editing a line or arrow is now included in history: entering or leaving edit mode can create an undo step, while changes that keep the same element being edited do not create a step just because the editor state changed.
Moving or removing a point on a line or arrow now uses the rough-rendered curve bounds to calculate its position, so point edits can affect the element’s placement as well as its points.

The drawing now keeps an ID-based lookup of all elements and provides a separate lookup that returns only elements that are not deleted; line and arrow editing uses the latter. The change making point lists read-only is type-level and has no direct user-visible effect.

Deleting while a line or arrow point is active now removes that point instead of deleting selected drawing objects; the edited element stays in point-editing mode unless it had fewer than two points, in which case it is removed.

Finalizing point editing now exits that mode and removes the element if it has fewer than two points or is invisibly small; Escape can also trigger finalization while point editing is active, including during a drag.

report.summary: The release overhauls live collaboration and editor integration to make shared drawings easier to set up, synchronize, and restore.
keyChanges: A new participant previously triggered a full initial scene broadcast; that explicit send is removed, so verify joining participants still receive the existing drawing.
Collaboration updates now use AES-GCM encryption with a newly generated 12-byte initialization value, and shared-scene loading handles encrypted data as well as legacy JSON.
Collaboration links are now recognized only when their URL hash exactly matches the room-and-key format, with letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens in each value.
Scene restoration now accepts null data and restores an empty scene with default settings instead of trying to read fields from missing data.
Drawing and collaboration setup now runs through the collaboration-aware editor wrapper, which handles saved drawings and incoming share links before supplying the scene to the editor.
Scene changes now reach live collaboration through the editor’s change callback, and pointer updates are passed to collaboration even during gestures with multiple active pointers.
The embeddable editor now defaults omitted dimensions to the browser window and exposes readiness, history, scrolling, and scene-reading controls through its editor reference.
Scene updates can omit drawing elements, include collaborator state, and request history recording; an initial-data promise that rejects is caught and the editor continues with an empty scene.
External drawings and collaboration links are initialized through the app’s scene-loading flow; an empty local drawing forces the link to load without an override prompt.
A collaboration link for the same room as one unloaded less than 15 seconds earlier also bypasses the override prompt; other non-empty local drawings still require confirmation.
Drawing changes are saved locally and broadcast during live collaboration, while joining a collaboration room loads its saved drawing or falls back to the live session.

The editor replaces its directly rendered room dialog with an optional collaboration button that invokes an action supplied by the host; when shown, it displays a collaborator count only when the count is greater than 0.

Collaboration cursor updates no longer include selected-element IDs, while the prior automatic scene-load shortcuts for an empty scene and reopening the same room within 15 seconds are removed; verify the resulting collaboration experience and load flow.

The main editor no longer contains its previous collaboration startup, remote-scene update, sharing, and unsaved-exit handling; verify that collaboration links, synchronized drawings, and unsaved changes still work.
The embeddable editor contract now allows optional dimensions and null or promise-based initial data, and exposes a readiness promise and status for its public API.
Flushing a debounced action before it has ever been called now does nothing instead of invoking it without saved arguments.

When two versions of the same drawing object have the same edit version but different tie-break values, collaboration now keeps one version instead of potentially dropping the object; verify that the drawing retains the selected version on both participants.
Scene updates now pass the syncable drawing snapshot from the collaboration caller, with full resyncs updating the tracked scene version; verify participants stay in sync during a live session.

Live pointer updates now take selected-element state from the editor, falling back to an empty selection when that state is unavailable, so collaboration should transmit the editor’s current selection.
The embeddable editor now forwards an editor ref and collaboration and pointer callbacks; an omitted collaboration-button callback defaults to a no-op.
Creating a room clears drawing history before sharing the current scene, while incoming collaborator changes update the drawing and clear undo history.
Drawing changes are broadcast when the scene version advances, and pointer updates are sent only when fewer than two pointers are active.
The collaboration dialog supports creating and ending a session, copying its link, and saving a changed username; ending a session saves the room and removes its room link from the address.

report.summary: The release improves how drawing elements connect and behave during canvas editing.
keyChanges: Canvas hit detection now uses element geometry and rotation to identify objects for selection, text editing, and context menus.

Arrow connections now support rectangle, diamond, ellipse, and text elements; connection updates cover moving or resizing connected elements and removing a connection without dropping a remaining link to the same shape.
Canvas hit testing now uses shape-relative distance checks with a 10-pixel-at-100%-zoom tolerance; this changes how clicks near shapes, text, and lines are recognized.

Arrow binding and its suggested highlight use a shape-size-based boundary: at least 15 pixels, at most 80 pixels, with diamond dimensions adjusted to align with rectangles; binding focus and gap are calculated for rectangles, text, diamonds, and ellipses.
Suggested arrow bindings now show a faint shape-boundary or endpoint highlight, and linear-point and rotation handles are drawn as filled circles.

New geometry operations underpin pointer hit-testing, shape transforms, line intersections, and arrow-to-shape connections, so verify that selecting and manipulating drawings and maintaining connections still work.
Arrows can suggest and form connections to shapes while being drawn or edited; holding Ctrl or Cmd disables binding, and changing tools can complete a connection at the arrow’s last point.
Pasting or inserting a copy now repairs connections between copied elements so an arrow can connect to its copied shape rather than the original.
Submitting an empty text edit removes the text and repairs connections that referred to it; canvas picking for selection, text editing, and context menus also uses a shared hit-testing path.
Arrows can connect to shapes, and their endpoints are recalculated when connected shapes move or resize; simple two-point arrows cannot connect both ends to the same shape.
The diamond-coordinate edit has no visible effect because the old and new left-edge coordinates are both zero.

report.summary: The release improves how text attached to shapes is displayed and handled throughout the drawing editor.
keyChanges: Text attached to a shape now wraps to the shape’s available width, and the shape can grow or shrink as the text changes; font and size changes also recalculate the text layout.
When finding a shape for text editing, existing text is ignored as a hit target so text inside a shape can be edited without treating that text as its own container.
Text editing can now reuse or create text attached to a shape, including when editing at the shape center; verify the text remains positioned within its shape.
Duplicating a shape with attached text now preserves the attachment on the copy, while attached text is excluded from ordinary hit-testing and marquee selection.
Text editor positioning now uses viewport coordinates directly, so editing with the canvas offset from the page should still place the editor over the text.
Resizing a shape with attached text now recalculates the text’s wrapping, position, and height, including when multiple elements are resized together.
A shape with attached text cannot be resized to negative dimensions, and its width must remain above the estimated minimum needed for a line of text.
Rotating a shape also rotates and repositions its attached text; adding text to a shape that is too small increases the shape to estimated minimum text dimensions.
Text wrapping now accounts for the available shape width and breaks overlong words across lines when needed.
Editing text attached to a shape now measures it within its current width and can expand the shape when the text exceeds its available space.
Copying a selected shape now includes its attached text, so both should be present when the copied drawing content is pasted.
Interior dragging now treats transparent fills differently: transparent shapes with attached text can be dragged from inside, while transparent shapes without attached text cannot.
Text already attached to a container is no longer eligible as a binding element, while standalone text remains eligible; this can affect arrow connections to text.
Selecting one rectangle, diamond, ellipse, or image now shows contextual guidance about binding text to it.
Text width measurement now uses canvas measurements and cached character widths, which may affect wrapping and the sizing of text attached to containers.
Clicking a shape to add text now targets its center, while starting text entry with one shape selected requests text binding; verify both ways of adding text to a shape.
Pasting, inserting from the Library, or drag-duplicating content now reconnects copied text to its copied shape; dragging an ungrouped shape also moves its attached text.

When adding selected content to the Library or exporting a selection, attached text is now included with its selected shape; pasted content selection also changes to include only standalone text elements.
Imported text missing attachment or original-text data now receives defaults of no attached shape and an empty original-text value.

report.summary: The release centralizes how selected drawing objects are retrieved across editing actions and canvas interactions.
keyChanges: Selection-dependent editing—such as aligning, distributing, grouping, copying, and editing frames or attached text—now obtains selections through the drawing scene, which also caches repeated selection lookups; verify that selected objects and their associated contents remain consistent across these actions.

Some canvas interactions previously looked up selections using a collection that included deleted objects, while the new lookup uses the current non-deleted scene; the practical effect for a user-created selection is not established.
qaChecks: Verify selecting multiple shapes and aligning or distributing them updates the intended shapes, and that grouping and ungrouping still act on the selection.
Check that copying selected shapes with attached text or frame contents includes the expected associated objects.
Confirm selecting one frame allows selecting its contents and removing all contents from the frame, without affecting unrelated objects.
Test selecting, dragging, resizing, and editing text or line points; confirm the visible selection and resulting edits apply to the intended non-deleted objects.

Check the changed edge case where a selected-object ID refers to a deleted object, if that state can be reached through normal editor use; confirm deleted objects are not acted on as current selections.
uncertainty: The changes consistently move selection lookups to the current non-deleted scene, but the supplied evidence does not establish a normal user action that produces a selected deleted object; whether that old-versus-new difference is user-reachable remains unclear.

report.summary: The release makes line and arrow editing more accurate and responsive, including for curves and shared changes.
keyChanges: Editing a multi-point line or arrow now exposes midpoint controls for its individual segments, and clicking a control inserts a point into that segment instead of at one overall midpoint.

For round lines and arrows with more than two points, midpoint placement and the short-segment threshold are based on the curved path; outside point-editing mode, midpoint controls are limited to elements with exactly two points.
The edited line or arrow’s point handles are now rendered from the visible drawing element during scene rendering, supporting alignment during live collaboration.

Rounded lines with more than two points now use their rendered curve to locate segment midpoints halfway by curve length and to measure segment length, affecting where editing handles appear and how short segments are treated.
Other lines continue to use straight-line midpoints and endpoint distances; point equality now requires both coordinates to match exactly.

Midpoint hover and insertion now target individual line segments, including curve-aware positions; previously the control used the line’s endpoint midpoint and was unavailable for lines with three or more points.
Pointer movement now reads the active editing state and returns without an edit result when no line is being edited. Navigation was not found in code.
qaChecks: Verify that a three-point line or arrow outside point-editing mode shows no midpoint controls, then enter point-editing mode and confirm each eligible segment has its own control.

Check a three-point line or arrow by clicking the midpoint of its second segment, away from the overall drawing midpoint; confirm a new point is inserted on that second segment and the other points remain in order.

Confirm that a round multi-point line or arrow’s midpoint control follows the curved segment, and that a segment whose curve length multiplied by zoom is below four point-handle sizes has no control while one at or above that threshold does.
Test editing a line or arrow during live collaboration while scene changes are synchronized; confirm its visible point handles stay aligned with the drawing.
Verify the curved two-point line’s midpoint control appears on the curve rather than at the midpoint between its endpoints, and that clicking the control inserts a point on that segment.
Check the three-point line and confirm each segment has its own midpoint control and that using one inserts a point on the chosen segment.
Confirm that moving the pointer over the canvas when no line is being edited leaves the drawing unchanged and the canvas usable.
Verify the segment midpoint handle for the curved line is positioned halfway along the visible curve, rather than at the straight midpoint between its endpoints.
Check that hovering over and selecting the curved segment's midpoint handle works at its displayed position.
uncertainty: The supplied changes add the curve calculations without showing the previous implementations, so the exact input that behaved differently before this change cannot be confirmed.

report.summary: Editing actions now consistently use the current drawing’s selection, with changes focused on selection-based operations.
keyChanges: Canvas interactions and selection-based editing now retrieve selected objects through the drawing scene, with explicit inclusion of frame contents and attached text retained where those options are requested.

Frame membership updates after selection operations, including alignment, distribution, and flipping, now resolve the selection against the supplied drawing elements. The diff does not establish a broader change to how these actions should behave.
Horizontal and vertical flips now pass the editor instance into frame-membership updates, allowing the update to use the current drawing selection.
Adding items to the Library now reads selected items from the current drawing scene, while continuing to include bound text and frame contents and to reject selections containing images.

The two selection-based zoom actions and contextual editing hints now get selected objects from the current scene instead of the element list passed to them, so verify zoom framing and selection hints remain appropriate.
Connector editing actions, context-menu labels, and keyboard selection handling now retrieve selected elements through the drawing scene while retaining the same stated selection options.
Pasted or inserted drawing items now pass editor context to selection handling; this supports selection processing after clipboard, library, and drop insertion.
The six alignment controls now check the editor scene’s selection; alignment remains available only for more than one selected non-frame object, so verify their availability and alignment results.

Lock availability, its context-menu label and shortcut, and the objects changed by locking now read the selection from the editor scene, retaining the existing handling of attached text and objects inside frames.

The six alignment operations now select objects from the editor’s current scene and pass the editor through frame-membership updates, so verify edge and center alignment also leaves selected objects correctly associated with their frames.
Copy, cut, text copying, and PNG/SVG clipboard exports now obtain selection from the current scene; attached text remains included, and object copying and image exports also include frame contents.

Grouping, ungrouping, and horizontal or vertical spacing now use the scene’s selected-object lookup; the visible selection criteria and spacing directions are otherwise unchanged in the supplied evidence.
Binding, unbinding, and wrapping text in a container now use the current scene’s selected elements; their existing selection requirements and resulting drawing changes are otherwise unchanged.
Selecting all elements in a frame and removing elements from a frame now use the current scene’s selection to determine whether one frame is selected and which frame to act on.

Check that selecting a frame along with another object does not make alignment controls available.
Verify that locking a selection that includes attached text or frame contents locks the selected objects and that toggling again unlocks them.

Check that aligning selected objects associated with a frame leaves their frame association consistent.
Verify copying or cutting the selection includes attached text and objects inside the frame.
Check PNG and SVG clipboard exports of a non-empty selection include its attached text and frame contents.

report.summary: This release changes how drawing updates are recorded for undo and redo, including updates from scene loading and live collaboration.
keyChanges: Drawing updates now distinguish captured changes, which create history increments, from snapshot-only updates; scene synchronization, image updates, and collaboration updates are explicitly marked as snapshot-only.

Before this change, an update with elements or app state was captured even when the old commit option was false; now an update with no store action does not update the history snapshot, so scene loading and integrations that omit the new option need focused checks.
qaChecks: Verify an integration sends an update containing one changed element while omitting the store-action option; confirm the element appears and check whether Undo treats the update as a recorded change, since the previous behavior captured it but the new behavior does not update the history snapshot.
Check that a normal drawing edit can be undone and redone, and that an update explicitly marked for snapshot-only handling does not become a separate undoable change.
Confirm a drawing change made by one participant appears for the other participant and remains present after ending the session and reopening the shared drawing.
Check that an image added during collaboration finishes loading and is visible to both participants.
uncertainty: The new store-action option is optional, but an update that omits it no longer changes the history snapshot; the supplied context does not establish whether integrations that omit the option are expected to remain undoable.

report.summary: The release improves canvas navigation and tool switching with hand-tool support across the editor.
keyChanges: The hand tool is available in the desktop and mobile toolbars; on desktop, H is its shortcut, and the tool changes the cursor and lets users pan the canvas.
While hand mode is active, shape actions are hidden when no elements are selected.
Finishing an eraser action now returns to the remembered active tool using the updated tool-state field; toolbar hints use a letter when a numeric shortcut is absent.
The editor toolbar now offers a hand-tool control on desktop and mobile, and the help dialog lists H as its shortcut.
Mobile toolbar controls are reordered: Library now appears before pen and lock controls, while the hand-tool control follows them.
Help-dialog shortcuts now capitalize a standalone lowercase single-character key; the supplied shortcuts do not show whether any currently displayed key uses that format.

The hand tool now routes a single-pointer drag into canvas panning and skips normal drawing interactions, so dragging the canvas in hand mode should move the view rather than create or alter an element.
The editor now connects a hand-tool control to its toggle action and supplies a hand icon; the exact control label is not provided.

Pressing H switches to the hand tool, clears the current element and group selection, and changes the cursor to a grab cursor; pressing H again restores the previous tool, or selection if none was saved.

Eraser switching now uses the shared previous-tool history, so turning it off should return to the tool active before the eraser; the evidence does not establish whether older editor state remains compatible.
When restoring a drawing saved with the hand tool active, restoration now permits that tool to remain active instead of treating it as an unlisted tool.

Check that switching from the hand tool to the eraser, completing an erase action, and finishing it returns to the hand tool.
Confirm that shape actions are hidden when hand mode is active and no elements are selected.
Verify that a toolbar tool with a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut displays the letter as its key hint.
Verify the desktop toolbar shows a hand-tool control and that selecting it makes its active state visible.
Verify the mobile toolbar shows the hand-tool control after the pen and lock controls, and that selecting it makes its active state visible.
Check the mobile toolbar order: Library appears before pen and lock, and the hand-tool control follows them.
Check the lock control while zen mode is enabled and confirm its intended visibility and toggling behavior.
Verify the tools section lists the hand tool with the H shortcut.
Confirm the existing shortcut entries remain legible and their key labels display as expected.
Verify that with the hand tool active, a left-button drag on the blank canvas pans the view and does not create an element.
Check that with the hand tool active, a left-button drag starting over an existing element pans the view instead of selecting or moving that element.
Verify pressing H while an element is selected clears the selection and changes the cursor to a grab cursor; press H again and confirm the prior drawing tool is restored.
Check the eraser toggle by pressing E while a drawing tool is active, then pressing E again; confirm the tool active before the eraser is restored.

uncertainty: The supplied evidence does not identify whether any actual toolbar tool has a letter shortcut but no numeric shortcut, so that hint fallback may not have a concrete item to test.

report.summary: The release refreshes sidebar behavior and related editor controls across the main and embedded editing experiences.
keyChanges: When restoring saved drawings, any string-valued sidebar setting now opens the default sidebar, even if the saved docking preference is false; previously only the Library setting could reopen, and only when docked.

Library updates that request the sidebar now open it on the Library tab, while updates without a confirmation prompt no longer automatically return keyboard focus to the editor; accepting a prompt still does.
The editor now takes keyboard focus on startup only when auto-focus is enabled, and the embeddable editor API can toggle a sidebar or force it open or closed.
The Library’s browsing and management controls are now grouped together, including in the empty-library state; removing items still clears the selection, and resetting still clears the Library.
The welcome screen’s center content and menu, toolbar, and help hints use updated wiring; their visible content is intended to remain available.
Buttons now support an active selected state, which applies selected styling when enabled.
The Library panel is now content within the default sidebar, and its control area groups browsing with library management options.
The default sidebar uses a saved docking preference, while custom integrations can supply their own docking behavior.
When host-provided UI is removed, the internal fallback can become available again instead of remaining suppressed.

Pasting, dropping, or inserting library items now keeps an open sidebar according to the default dock preference rather than its current docked state; the new element-insertion capability places supplied elements at the canvas center.
Sidebar control now uses a sidebar name and optional tab instead of the previous library/custom-sidebar toggle, and no longer explicitly rejects a custom sidebar when no renderer is configured.
Confirming or cancelling through a confirmation dialog now returns focus to the editor container, including clear-canvas and library removal or reset confirmations.
Shared buttons now run a supplied click handler before their selection action, skip that action when the handler prevents the default, and apply selected styling when selected.
Sidebar content now renders only for the active sidebar, and selecting a tab updates the active tab; sidebar triggers control whether their sidebar is open.
Outside clicks and Escape close an undocked sidebar, or one that does not fit the device, unless a dialog is open; a docked sidebar that fits stays open.
The dock control appears only when the device can fit the sidebar and docking is configured, while closing a sidebar no longer invokes its supplied close notification.
The editor now shows its default sidebar instead of choosing between the previous library menu and a host-provided custom sidebar, changing which sidebar content appears when a sidebar is open.
On mobile, the scroll-back control is now hidden whenever any sidebar is open; on desktop, a docked sidebar reserves space beside the drawing.
Choosing a chart preview now inserts its elements through the editor’s shared insertion path and closes the paste dialog.

Custom sidebars now use editor-provided sidebar content, triggers, and named tabs instead of the former sidebar-render callback; the package also exposes its default sidebar, so integrations relying only on the old callback need to migrate.
On devices too narrow for a sidebar, editing tips are now hidden whenever any sidebar is open, rather than only when the Library sidebar is open.
The previous Library toolbar control implementation is removed; its replacement and continued availability are not established, so verify how editors reach their reusable drawing Library.
The sidebar header no longer includes its previous dock toggle, while its close action now uses a close-request callback; verify docking and closing remain available as intended.

Check that loading data with only the older Library-open preference set to true does not reopen the sidebar.

Confirm that accepting a library confirmation prompt returns keyboard focus to the editor.

Verify the empty Library shows its browsing and management controls when there are no saved items and no pending elements.
Check that selecting and removing a saved item removes it from the Library and clears the selection.
Confirm that resetting a populated Library clears its saved items.
Confirm pressing Escape while the sidebar is undocked still closes the Library, as it did before this change.
Verify the welcome-screen center content and its menu, toolbar, and help guidance appear in their expected positions.
Check that a button presented as selected shows its active styling, and that the unselected state does not show that styling.
Verify the Library tab shows its browsing and management controls, and that inserting a Library item adds it to the drawing.
Check the undocked sidebar by clicking outside it; confirm it closes as it did before the Library panel moved into the default sidebar.
Confirm changing the default sidebar’s docked state is reflected in its saved docking preference when the sidebar is shown again.
Verify that after host-provided UI has been mounted and then removed, rendering the editor without that host UI displays the internal fallback.
Verify that pasting, dropping, or inserting elements while the sidebar is open, the device can fit it, and the current state is docked but the default preference is false closes the sidebar.
Check that submitting elements through the embedded-editor insertion capability places them at the canvas center.
Verify that requesting the custom sidebar to open is accepted and reports success when no renderer is configured.
Check that choosing either confirm or cancel closes the confirmation and returns focus to the editor container.

Confirm the dock control appears only when docking is configured on a device that can fit the sidebar, and that selecting it toggles the docked state.

Test a button with a click handler that prevents the default: the handler should run, the button’s selection action should not, and a button marked selected should show selected styling; confirm closing an embedded sidebar does not invoke its supplied close notification.
Verify that the default reusable-drawing sidebar opens from its toolbar trigger and can be docked and undocked on desktop and mobile.

The supplied evidence removes the Library toolbar component and its previous sidebar-header docking control but does not establish their replacement or whether those capabilities are intentionally removed.

report.summary: The release standardizes how drawing and image changes are tracked, saved, undone, and synchronized across editing and collaboration.
keyChanges: Already-observed editor state is now recognized and reused rather than projected again, which should preserve observed selection details when state updates are recorded.
Unchanged observed elements or editor state reuse the existing snapshot, avoiding a new recorded increment when there is no detected change.

Canvas interactions now distinguish updates to the current history snapshot from changes captured for undo and redo, so short touch-drawing cleanup and other transient edits should not become separate undo steps.
Choosing a color with the eyedropper now records the selection as a captured drawing change, while completed editor updates are committed after rendering.
Importing an Excalidraw drawing updates the existing drawing’s history snapshot before adding imported content, helping preserve element ordering when undoing.

Image save and failure status changes, and scene refreshes synchronized from another browser tab, are now applied as scene updates; loading a scene after a URL change is explicitly captured, while ordinary scene loading no longer explicitly disables store commits.
Line and arrow point editing has no identified runtime behavior change.

Incoming and initial collaboration scenes, session-stop updates, and completed shared-image uploads now explicitly use the UPDATE store action; verify drawings and shared images remain intact and synchronized in these flows.
The exported store-action values are now lowercase (“capture”, “update”, and “none”) instead of uppercase, so integrations using literal values must update them.
Store updates are now committed according to scheduled actions, with capture taking precedence over a snapshot-only update; resetting the store also clears queued actions.
qaChecks: Verify the selected line or arrow remains selected after an editor-state update and that undoing and redoing the drawing edit restores the expected drawing state.
Verify a very short touch-drawn freehand mark that records fewer than 10 points, followed by placing a second finger, is discarded and does not return as a separate change when undoing.
Check that resizing an element and then undoing and redoing leaves the drawing in the corresponding before-and-after states.
Confirm that choosing a color with the eyedropper updates the selected element, or the current drawing color when no element is selected, and that undo and redo reverse and reapply the color change.
Verify that importing the drawing and then undoing and redoing preserves the distinct ordering of existing and imported elements.
Verify that an element update without a specified history action appears on the canvas, and check whether it creates a new undo step.
Verify that loading the scene URL replaces the current drawing and that the loaded drawing is available to undo, as expected for a captured scene change.
Check that when the image file is unavailable, the image remains in the drawing with its error state and the status refresh does not create a separate undoable drawing edit.
Confirm that after saving an image, its saved status appears without creating a separate undoable drawing edit.
Verify that when the second tab receives the newer saved scene, the drawing refreshes without treating the synchronization itself as a new user edit.

report.summary: The release improves how people discover and use editor actions while refining related editing and dialog interactions.
keyChanges: Shortcut lookup can now return a requested alternate shortcut, falling back to the first when that index is unavailable; the Ctrl/Cmd+P hint can therefore show the second shortcut instead of repeating the first.

The command palette’s supplied implementation supports keyboard navigation, marks unavailable commands, and closes before running a selected command; its displayed labels and icons can reflect the current drawing.
Dialogs now focus their initial control after a delay, and the header close button appears only on mobile, where it uses a close icon.
Double-clicking a selected line or arrow that is already being edited now continues through regular canvas double-click handling instead of returning early.

Ctrl+P or Cmd+P without Shift or Alt now shows a temporary command-palette shortcut hint, the help dialog lists the command-palette shortcuts, and a command-palette menu item is configured to open the palette.
Context-action captions now use the action’s general label instead of its context-specific caption, so actions that supply only the older context-specific caption may have no displayed caption.
Dialogs now receive disabled-animation styling when animation disabling is active when the dialog first opens, and external links are opened with opener access disabled.
The command palette groups commands in a defined order and supports fuzzy, accent-insensitive search; searches discard spaces and the characters <, >, -, _, and | before matching.

The palette exposes stroke- and background-color commands when the current selection supports them, using the same eligibility rules as the selection controls; running a command opens its corresponding color popup.

The command palette is added to the main menu and gains actions for sharing, live collaboration, Excalidraw+ promotion and export, community links, and theme switching; signed-in users see a combined Excalidraw+ sign-in or destination option instead of the separate promotion and sign-up options.
Element-lock actions now require a selection to toggle locking, show wording and an icon based on the selection, and offer unlock-all only when nothing is selected and at least one element is locked.
Opening another editor dialog now closes the share or collaboration dialog.

Editor actions now include display labels and icons, with palette names for canvas background, clearing, and hand-tool actions; theme switching gains dark/light search keywords, a theme-dependent action label and icon, and a command that runs the registered theme action.
Choosing the image tool from the command palette by keyboard sets direct insertion on, while choosing it by mouse does not.
When no element is selected, hyperlink label generation now safely resolves to the create-link label; the hyperlink action itself is available only when exactly one element is selected.

report.summary: The release changes how drawing edits and editor actions are recorded and restored, with undo and redo behavior the main area to verify.
keyChanges: Deleting the last remaining point of an edited line now captures the deletion in history; before, this case did not capture it, so undo should restore the line.
Text attached to a rotated container now takes on the container’s angle when its bounding box is redrawn, so verify its orientation after editing or changing its layout.

Connection handling now revisits bound text and arrows when elements change or are removed, including resolving competing bound text; verify connections and attached text after edits, deletion, undo, and redo.

Grouping and ungrouping now capture successful changes in the drawing store, and grouping uses the reordered elements returned by the ordering step; verify group order and that undo restores the prior drawing.

Undo and redo now track drawing and app-state changes separately; unlike before, an app-state-only change no longer clears redo, so edits such as changing the canvas background should not discard a pending redo.
Loading a scene after a URL hash change now commits it to the drawing store rather than recording it as a history change.
When the drawing has no undo or redo entries, the corresponding control is now disabled; previously it remained enabled and clicking it made no change.

Undo and redo now apply recorded drawing and app-state changes against the current scene snapshot, including resolving affected element bindings; verify edits can still be reversed and reapplied without losing visible drawing relationships.
Undo and redo now apply drawing and editor-state changes together, including element order, bindings, and text attached to shapes; verify that restored edits remain visually consistent.

History application now reconciles selected shapes, groups, and line-editing state against elements that still exist, removing references to deleted items and restoring state when the related item exists.

Scene snapshots now detect changes to elements and observed editor state, preserve missing elements as deletions, and capture increments when changes are detected; this also reaches scene loading and has potential relevance to collaboration.

Pasting drawing content or text, erasing, editing line points, changing selected colors, importing drawings, and removing frame contents now request history capture; frame selection changes are captured too.
After undo, a selection-only change no longer clears redo, and a pointer-up that changes the selection can now be recorded even when nothing remains selected.

report.summary: The release adds elbow arrows and improves how they connect, route, and respond to editing and undo.
keyChanges: Elbow arrows now have logic to choose a route around shapes and to update that route as endpoints or intermediate points are edited, or as connected shapes move, resize, or rotate.
Connection logic accounts for rotated shapes, distinguishes diamond sides, and snaps dragged endpoints toward shape edges or midpoints; navigation was not found in the supplied context.
Elbow-arrow connections can now treat a point inside a shape’s bounds as a binding target while the arrow is being dragged, not only points on or near its outline.

Elbow arrows now render with rounded bends, up to 16 units of corner radius and limited to half the length of either adjoining segment; corner routing and connected-arrow transforms also receive updated handling.
New elbow-arrow routing chooses a path around drawing elements; newly created arrows default to the round arrow type.
Undo and redo now recalculate arrows connected to changed elements using the current drawing, which can affect the restored connector route.

Arrow tools and selected arrows now offer arrow-style controls; pressing A while the arrow tool is active cycles sharp, round, and elbow styles, while arrows no longer offer roundness changes and elbow arrows are excluded from the line-point editor.
Elbow arrows now route around drawing elements and can bind to shapes; unlike before, moving a single bound elbow arrow by dragging, resizing it, or pressing an arrow key does not move it.
Elbow-arrow point editing no longer snaps to the grid, and box selection of their points is limited to the two endpoints.
The arrow-tool hint now gives arrow-specific guidance including the A shortcut; line-tool and multi-segment guidance remain distinct.

Elbow-arrow connections now use fixed attachment points, and resizing a connected shape or duplicating its arrow preserves the full connection details; verify attachments remain at the same relative point.
Elbow arrows no longer show rotation handles or a bounding box, and their editing handles and point highlights omit interior route points while retaining the endpoints.
Elbow-arrow routing now adjusts snap points to avoid rectangular corners, and binding previews use a fixed 10-pixel outline thickness instead of a shape-dependent thickness.
Negative angles now convert to a 0–360° range: for example, -90° previously produced -90° and now produces 270°.
Elbow arrows no longer expose the rotation control in the Stats panel, and rotation edits there skip elbow arrows.
Changing element position or size through the Stats panel now supplies the drawing context when updating connector bindings, including when resizing groups.
When restoring a drawing, elbow-arrow status is retained and a missing binding fixed point defaults to [0,0]; non-elbow bindings have their fixed point cleared.
Arrow skeletons are now created as arrows, and arrow containers are recognized for binding during conversion.

Arrow properties now offer sharp, round, and elbow styles; converting an arrow to elbow style keeps its endpoints and recalculates its route, while switching away from elbow style also starts from those endpoints.
Elbow arrows are excluded from the straight-line editor and no longer accept segment midpoints; the general roundness setting also no longer changes elbow arrows.
Arrow connections are recalculated during drawing, editing, flipping, and property-panel moves, resizes, and rotations so connectors can stay attached to shapes.

Elbow arrows are created with two endpoints, route as users draw, and finalize instead of accepting another bend point; with grid snapping enabled, their drawing points are no longer snapped to the grid.
Deleting a shape connected to an elbow arrow now clears that connection and recalculates the arrow route; cutting a selected shape follows the same deletion behavior.
Undo and redo now recalculate connected-arrow routes when restoring drawing changes.
Ctrl+double-clicking a selected elbow arrow no longer follows the special path that opens point editing.

report.summary: The release expands drawing-editor selection with lasso tools and refines related drawing interactions and controls.
keyChanges: Ellipse outlines used four unique straight chords, duplicated, for geometry checks; they are now represented by a closed 90-segment approximation, which can change whether lasso strokes and frame edges intersect an ellipse.

Lasso selection now checks element outlines for enclosure or intersection, applies a tolerance of 1 to intersection checks, and normalizes selection so bound text selects its container and selecting a frame omits its children. The prior behavior of these newly supplied lasso routines cannot be established from the available evidence.
Lasso feedback now uses an animated, dashed indigo trail that is cleared when the gesture ends; updating a trail also discards previously completed trails, including laser-pointer trails.
Dragging a new shape while holding the center-resize modifier no longer draws it outward from its center; it uses the initial pointer position as its origin instead.

Lasso gestures now update selection as the path is drawn, clear the existing selection when started without Shift, and preserve it when started with Shift; the trail and selection state are cleared when the gesture ends.
Holding Alt while dragging an existing selection box now switches to lasso selection; releasing Alt during that drag returns to box selection instead of continuing the lasso.
Restoration now recognizes lasso in its tool map, so imported drawing state with lasso selected should retain that tool instead of treating it as unrecognized.

Line-segment intersection checks now accept an optional tolerance; a crossing 0.5 units beyond a segment endpoint can count as an intersection when the supplied tolerance is 1, while existing callers shown do not supply a tolerance.

The lasso tool can be selected from the extra-tools menu or command palette, and the selection tool button switches to lasso when selection is already active; verify the tool shown as active matches the choice.
With lasso active, shape actions are hidden when nothing is selected but remain available when elements are selected; releasing Space no longer clears an existing selection.
Two canvas hints are now displayed as a one-item hint list, which removes a final period if the translated hint includes one; the embed tool symbol also has a slightly heavier outline.
A new lasso tool lets editors select drawing elements by enclosing or intersecting them; activating it clears the current selection, and activating it again returns to the selection tool.

Explicit custom names are removed from the canvas background, clear canvas, hand tool, unlock-all, statistics, view mode, and zen mode actions; the effect on how those actions are found is not established.

Verify that when the displayed canvas-panning or deep-selection hint ends in a period, the displayed hint has no final period; also confirm the embed tool symbol remains clear with its slightly heavier outline.

report.summary: The release improves device-aware selection behavior and tool recovery across the editor.
keyChanges: On touch-capable devices with a coarse pointer, lasso is the default selection tool; after pasting or inserting items, creating text, or finishing a drawing, the editor now returns to that default instead of always returning to selection.

Lasso interaction now distinguishes taps on elements from lasso gestures: touch users select an unselected element immediately and can drag it, while desktop users avoid moving elements accidentally during a lasso gesture.
In lasso mode, Ctrl+Alt pointer-down now starts a lasso trail and switches to lasso selection; touch context menus and canvas double-click handling are also allowed when lasso is the default tool.

When lasso is the default selection tool, it takes the primary selection-tool position and the 1 shortcut; the separate lasso menu item is hidden, and returning from the laser tool or unlocking a tool returns to lasso.
With lasso active and no elements selected, hovering over a movable element no longer shows the move cursor; the move cursor remains available when elements are selected.
Pasting copied drawing elements on mobile or tablet now places them at the canvas center instead of at the cursor; desktop placement remains at the cursor.
The welcome screen on an empty drawing now appears when the default selection tool is active, including when that tool is lasso.
On mobile or tablet, a restored selection, lasso, or image tool now becomes lasso; on desktop, a restored lasso now becomes selection, while selection and image resolve to selection.
After image selection is canceled or fails, the editor now returns to its device’s default tool instead of always returning to selection.

After clearing the canvas from the image tool, deleting selected elements, or finishing an interaction, the editor now returns to its configured default selection tool instead of always returning to standard selection; leaving the eraser with no saved prior tool follows that same default.

The lasso-tool action is suppressed when lasso is already the default, and snapping can now operate during a drag of selected elements with lasso active, while remaining disabled during lasso selection itself.
iOS platform detection now ignores letter case, and a mobile-device classification has been added; this may affect which resize and rotation handles are available on mobile devices.

report.summary: This release changes how framed drawings are targeted, ordered, and displayed during editing.
keyChanges: Frame targeting now accounts for the topmost object and existing frame membership, while dragged selections are previewed in frame order before the drop is committed.
New objects and pasted framed drawings are inserted with frame-child ordering in mind; text bound to a container no longer joins a frame unless that container belongs to it.
Interior hit testing now treats a non-transparent color as a filled background only for element types that support backgrounds.

report.summary: The release refines keyboard-driven flowchart creation and navigation in the drawing editor.
keyChanges: Ctrl/Command+Arrow creation and Alt+Arrow navigation are handled together; when creation commits, the new elements are inserted and the first is selected and brought into view if needed.
When navigation and creation end on the same key release, both workflows are cleared and an immediate history capture is requested once, rather than separately for each workflow.

Newly created flowchart nodes are positioned to avoid space occupied by connected nodes, rather than always using the previous evenly spaced layout; repeated additions in a blocked direction may appear in a different open position.
Keyboard navigation between linked nodes now uses the direction of their elbow-arrow connections, and canceling creation clears its saved placement position.

New flowchart nodes are placed one 100-pixel gap along the chosen direction and shifted to the nearest clear cross-axis slot, accounting for obstacles throughout the connected flowchart rather than only nearby linked nodes.
When a pending group of nodes grows, its existing nodes are intended to keep their positions if the larger group still fits.
The creator’s initial direction changes from right to unset, and the former fallback that mapped unrecognized keys to right is removed; the expected keyboard behavior needs confirmation.

Undo and redo still defer history updates while a flowchart is being created, and the editor still receives pending flowchart nodes; these values are now accessed through the flowchart state holder. The diff does not establish a change to what users see or how they create diagrams.

Check that extending a pending group from one node to two in clear space leaves the first node in its original position.

report.summary: The release expands text-to-diagram creation into a chat-based workflow with improved diagram previews and related interface behavior.
keyChanges: Text-to-diagram chat now supports prompt entry, saved-chat management, message actions, generated-diagram preview and insertion, and Mermaid viewing; the chat area also shows remaining message limits and generated responses can be opened as Mermaid.

The send button is enabled only when the trimmed prompt has more than 3 characters, but pressing Enter submits any nonblank prompt; Shift+Enter adds a line break, and submitting trims and clears the prompt.
Actions explicitly marked disabled are now unavailable; during generation, the new-chat and chat-history controls are disabled, and network-error retry becomes available after the 5-second wait.

Saved chats are stored locally, sorted by update time, limited to the 10 most recently updated chats, and titled from the first user message; titles are trimmed and messages longer than 50 characters become the first 47 characters followed by an ellipsis.
Preview errors now have a localized title and can show a generic Mermaid syntax message instead of parser details; the preview canvas is hidden when an error is present.
Workflow panels can show multiple button, link, or rate-limit actions, affecting chat actions and the diagram preview’s insert action.

Chat management now supports starting a fresh chat, restoring saved chats, and deleting chats; deleting the active chat switches to the first remaining saved chat or starts a blank chat if none remain.

Saved chats are applied with message timestamps normalized, and the active error state is restored from the last assistant message; chats are saved when message history changes and generation is not active.

Mermaid previews now validate and throttle streaming content, flush pending content when generation finishes, and render the latest assistant message when switching chats; a chat with no assistant messages clears the preview.

Text-to-diagram generation now sends chat messages to a streaming service, combines streamed content into the generated diagram, and handles rate-limit and stream errors; an HTTP 429 now returns “Rate limit exceeded” instead of the previous daily-limit message.
Mermaid preview rendering now rejects empty text, mismatched brackets, braces, or parentheses, and text ending with an incomplete diagram operator or separator.

Mermaid conversion now returns a success or failure result, uses the supplied editor theme for its preview, and no longer checks the rendered canvas by converting it to a blob; test oversized diagrams and conversion failures.
Dialogs no longer carry the outside-click prevention marker, so check that backdrop dismissal and clicks inside dialog content behave as intended.
The command palette’s clock symbol is replaced by a history-style symbol, and the code-family symbol in font selection is updated.
Text-to-diagram prompts must contain 3–10,000 characters, and generation is blocked when no requests remain.

Generation adds the prompt and a pending assistant reply to chat, sends the three most recent non-empty chat messages plus the current prompt, streams the reply, and attempts to convert it into a diagram.
Request failures distinguish rate-limit warnings from exhausted-message-limit warnings; Mermaid parsing errors are reported in chat, with nested error messages displayed on separate lines.
An aborted generation is not reported as a request or parsing failure.

The current chat handling adds and updates messages, selects the latest assistant reply, and excludes empty content from generation context; prior implementations are not supplied, so these cannot be confirmed as behavior changes.
Text-to-diagram is now presented as a chat workflow with chat history and actions to retry or repair a response, view it as Mermaid, and insert a diagram into the drawing.
The Mermaid preview now renders and saves edits only while its tab is active, clears when its active input is empty, and uses the editor’s current theme.
Deleting an assistant reply truncates the chat before the prompt immediately preceding that reply, so later messages may also be removed.

report.summary: The release improves frame-aware drawing and editing, including element placement, visual feedback, and browser support.
keyChanges: Canvas hit-testing now treats a nontransparent background as fill only for element types that support backgrounds; previously any element with a nontransparent background could be treated as filled, affecting clicks inside elements and which overlapping elements can receive arrow connections.

Frame highlighting now uses an explicit eligible-type list, and deselecting or finishing an element clears the highlight; verify permitted drawing tools can still highlight frames and stale highlights disappear.
Browsers missing several standard array methods now receive fallbacks, supporting the editor in those environments.
Adding a mixed selection to a frame now reorders already-contained elements together with newly added elements, while keeping attached text with its shape.
A single frame-associated element is now inserted at the end of the drawing order instead of at the frame’s position; batch insertion’s replacement behavior is not shown in the supplied changes.
Library-item copies and drops now use a frame-duplication path that preserves the original ordering of frame contents, so overlapping objects may stack differently from before.

Frame membership now considers the topmost object under the pointer, and dragging an existing frame child can retain its current frame; placement over an unrelated object above a frame can therefore differ from the previous topmost-frame-only behavior.

Text creation now checks the text’s final placement and gives a bindable container priority over a frame; frame highlights are also refreshed when new elements are inserted and cleared when the active tool changes.
Pasting or dropping drawing items now preserves the order of items inside copied frames; verify copied frame contents remain in their original order.
New elements, including pasted text, images, and embeddable items, are inserted in frame-aware positions rather than always being added at the end of the drawing.
Moving the pointer can update which frame is highlighted, except while creating or dragging elements or when the pointer is over a scrollbar.
The drawing renderer now selects which in-progress element to show on the preview canvas, so verify new elements display correctly as they are created.

report.summary: The release updates how the service starts, reloads data, and validates and handles requests.
keyChanges: Starting with a missing .json database source now creates that file with bundled example data before loading it; router setup errors are now printed and cause the process to exit with status 1.
Editing the watched routes file now restarts the server, while database and routes watching now use native directory file events instead of the previous watcher library.
Collection filters now skip records when the matched field is falsy, including numeric 0; zero-value searches may no longer return records they matched before.

Create and update requests no longer convert numeric-looking body strings to numbers, and individual-record lookups and deletions no longer convert URL IDs before matching. GET collection responses also build pagination links using a URL formatter; no changed link behavior is established by the evidence.

Request parsing and method override are now attached to the database router rather than the shared default middleware; method override runs before body parsing, which may affect requests that supply the override in a form body.

When a collection already contains a nonnumeric identifier, the next generated identifier changes from a UUID to a shortid-generated string; empty collections still start at 1 and numeric identifiers still increment.
Database contents are now validated during router setup, but the validation rules and resulting error behavior are not specified in the supplied evidence.

Nested GET and POST requests now pass the parent ID through unchanged instead of converting values such as "true" to booleans or numeric strings such as "1" to numbers; verify downstream filtering and association use the literal string.
New validation code accepts only plain objects and rejects top-level property names containing "/"; its connection to a runnable request path is not established.
Launching the new command-line entry point invokes the existing CLI argument handling; the remaining edits preserve the prior behavior.
qaChecks: Verify starting with a missing .json database path creates the file with bundled example data and starts the server.
Check that editing the watched routes file restarts the server and loads the updated routes; before this change, the edit was only logged.
Test replacing the watched JSON database file atomically with different contents and confirm the server reloads.
Verify a collection filter with the precise input score=0 still returns the record whose score is 0; this input matched before but is skipped by the new falsy-value check.
Check a request that creates or updates a record with the precise body value {"count":"7"} preserves count as the string "7", rather than converting it to the number 7.
Confirm an existing record with numeric ID 7 remains retrievable and deletable when its URL ID is "7".
Verify a URL-encoded request containing _method=DELETE is still treated as a DELETE request, as it was when body parsing ran before method override.
Confirm a database containing arrays or objects of records starts successfully and remains available for requests after startup validation.
Check that adding a record to a collection whose existing identifier is a string produces a shortid-generated string identifier rather than a UUID-shaped identifier.
Verify a nested GET using parent ID "true" filters by the literal string "true", not the boolean true.
Verify a nested POST using parent ID "1" associates the submitted record with the literal string "1", not the number 1.
Check that a plain object containing property "a/b" is rejected with an error identifying the unsupported slash in the property name.
Check that an array input is rejected because the data must be an object.
Verify launching the entry point with a source argument reaches the existing CLI argument handling.
uncertainty: The exact database input that makes router setup fail is not specified, so the new error-and-exit behavior has no concrete rejection case to verify from the supplied evidence; native file-watch event handling may also vary by platform.

The application context provides no API routes or navigation, and does not document whether numeric-looking body values are intended to remain strings; confirm that expectation. The changed lookup and filtering behavior also creates a regression risk for numeric IDs and zero-valued fields, which the checks should resolve.

Because method override now runs before form-body parsing, a URL-encoded _method=DELETE may no longer be recognized; verify this against the prior behavior. The supplied evidence also does not define startup validation rules or show whether consumers of the default middleware separately install the newly exported parsers.

No affected application surfaces or dependency paths are supplied for the new validation code or the removed JSON-file detection helper, so whether either is reachable through a user-facing flow cannot be confirmed.
No application navigation or role information was supplied, and there is no prior entry-point behavior to compare for a changed input boundary.
